notes.note: 2026-09-20 13:3xZ ops-triage: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED in-repo, then auto-closed. This key fired at 09:25 EDT on a LIVE instance, not residue: pid 24411 (owner=foreign, cgroup tmux-spawn-484a16ae..., started 08:57) is an interactive ComfyUI on the shared install mid-render -- /history showed 5 prompts 09:00:52->09:25:53Z (each ~57 s, 7 images), the newest 4 min before the probe, and the growth brain's 09:04 tick independently mislabelled the same pid an 'orphan/leak'. Acting on that label means killing a human's render session, which the harness ownership rule forbids. Fix: bin/tc_ops.py check_comfyui_vram_unclaimed now gates on the instance's own liveness (native /queue depth + newest /history prompt timestamp, COMFYUI_LIVE_WINDOW_S=1800) -- live or unreadable => no issue; only idle-and-abandoned files, and its evidence now names the holder (owner/pid/cgroup/started) so a human can shut it down from its own session. Verified both ways: selftest 112 assertions 0 failures (9 new comfyui_holder_verdict cases); live check() -> None at last_prompt_age 42 s; synthetic idle -> warn with full attribution; queue non-empty and curl-failure -> None; probe run re-evaluated and auto-closed this key. Commit ce875f3.

2026-09-23 05:4xZ ops-triage: DECIDED -- accept the hold (yield), and made the check's claim TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION. Condition is real: pid 553489 (holder=operator, his byobu/tmux session, started Tue Sep 22 18:49 EDT) is IDLE (native queue empty, last prompt 62 min) holding 18,438 of the card's 18,945 MiB with no claim and no --reserve-vram. But the title asserted that from the CARD-level reading (nvidia-smi memory.used = an upper bound counting every co-tenant), so a labeler holding 14 GiB beside an idle ComfyUI holding 300 MiB produced the same reading AND the same title -- a false attribution that sends a reader to shut down the wrong process. FIX (bin/tc_ops.py): new pure unclaimed_vram_verdict(card_mib, own_mib) + comfyui_instance_vram_mib() (per-pid, --query-compute-apps): the instance's OWN hold decides; a co-tenant's VRAM makes the check quiet; an unreadable own-hold keeps the detection but is worded as the card's, never the instance's. Verified: selftest 451/0 (9 new branches: co-tenant-holds-it -> quiet, own-unreadable -> still fires); live re-run prints 'the instance itself holds 18438MiB of the card's 18945MiB' and still fires. DECISION: YIELD -- a foreign operator session is not ours to kill or re-flag; the render impact is render-starved's warn, and that refusal is over-determined (launch-args gate first, then free 5.0GiB < 16GiB floor). Escalation criterion unchanged (pre-registered by the overnight watchdog): dry_out inside ~3 days while refusals continue -- currently 09-29T10:30Z (6.3d), so no Tim ask.
